ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the parabola $y=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}+bx+c$ (where $b$ and $c$ are constants) has its vertex at the coordinates $\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{25}{8}\right)$, intersects the $x$-axis at points $A$ and $B$ (with point $A$ to the left of point $B$), and intersects the $y$-axis at point $C$. Point $C$ and point $D$ are symmetric about the $x$-axis. Connect $AD$ and draw line $BD$. What are the values of $b$ and $c$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the parabola $y=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}+bx+c$ has its vertex at $\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{25}{8}\right)$,\\
thus, the equation of the parabola is $y=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\frac{3}{2}\right)^{2}-\frac{25}{8}$\\
Simplifying, we obtain $y=\frac{1}{2}x^{2}-\frac{3}{2}x-2$,\\
thus, $b=\boxed{-\frac{3}{2}}$ and $c=\boxed{-2}$.
